title: Back to the Busan Basics - The Wire China
gist: Paywalled teaser on the U.S.-China trade truce reached in Busan in late October 2025, ahead of a second Trump-Xi meeting this year in Washington; argues the clock is ticking on the truce.

insights.claim: The U.S.-China trade war truce agreed in Busan, South Korea in late October 2025 is time-limited, and its expiry is approaching as Trump and Xi prepare for a second meeting in Washington.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Truce expiry is a tariff-risk catalyst for supply chains and China-exposed equities.
insights.quote: As Presidents Trump and Xi gear up for their second meeting this year in Washington, the clock is ticking on their trade war truce.

insights.claim: The Busan agreement paused a trade war that had upended U.S.-China relations and rattled global supply chains, and the White House at the time called it a massive victory.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The truce's framing as a win raises political stakes for extending it rather than letting tariffs snap back.
insights.quote: paused the trade war that had upturned U.S.-China relations and rattled global supply chains
insights.locator: The agreement reached in late October

insights.claim: A White House fact sheet dated November 1, 2025 codified the U.S.-China trade and economic deal terms, serving as the reference baseline for assessing compliance before the next summit.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: Compliance against the fact sheet terms will likely determine whether the truce is renewed.
insights.locator: An excerpt from a fact sheet
